rows.name: ENABLE_FUSE_STATS
rows.table: 5.1 `GNUmakefile` and the scripts that it runs

cells.Set by: Developers who build without FUSE stats.
cells.Values and default: Text for the CMake option `ENABLE_FUSE_STATS`, for example `ON` or `OFF`. The makefile passes the text without a check. `make ENABLE_FUSE_STATS=OFF` also works. Unset: `ON`. Empty: the makefile passes the empty text to CMake, and CMake counts empty text as off.
cells.Effect: Selects at CMake configure time whether FUSE stats are compiled into the programs. `GNUmakefile` passes the text to `cmake` as `-DENABLE_FUSE_STATS=<value>`. A changed value rewrites the file `gen/.fuse_stats_stamp`, and `make` then runs CMake configure again. `GNUmakefile` passes the value only for builds in `gen/` and for `make deb`. The sanitizer, coverage and `deb-host` builds do not get it. For a build on an LSF worker (`REMOTE`), a `make` command-line value and a non-empty environment value reach the worker.

rows.name: FUSE_STATS_STAMP
rows.table: 5.1 `GNUmakefile` and the scripts that it runs

cells.Values and default: File path. This is an internal make variable. `GNUmakefile` assigns it and ignores an environment value, except when the only goals are `list-tests` or `list-tests-core`. Unset: `gen/.fuse_stats_stamp`. When the only goals are `list-tests` or `list-tests-core`, the text is empty.
cells.Effect: An environment value changes no build result. For the goals `list-tests` and `list-tests-core` alone, `make` puts the value into the prerequisite lists of the CMake configure targets and the package target. `make` does not build those targets for these goals. The file holds the last `ENABLE_FUSE_STATS` value. A changed file makes `make` run CMake configure again. `make FUSE_STATS_STAMP=path` on the command line replaces the path for every goal.

rows.name: HAS_AVX512
rows.table: 5.1 `GNUmakefile` and the scripts that it runs

cells.Values and default: Only the text `no` has an effect. On Linux the makefile assigns `yes` or `no` itself and ignores an environment value. On macOS it uses the environment value. Unset: on Linux, `yes` when `/proc/cpuinfo` lists the flag `avx512f`, otherwise `no`. On macOS, empty text.
cells.Effect: `no` means that the CPU of the build host lacks AVX-512 (a CPU instruction set). `make t_<name>` then builds the test and stops with an error before the run. When `REMOTE` is `0`, `test`, `test-core`, `test-host`, `test-fpga`, `test-fast` and `test-proxy` stop with an error and build nothing. `make HAS_AVX512=value` on the command line replaces the detected value on Linux too. The `-old` test targets stop in the same way. The sanitizer and coverage targets do not check the variable.

The `-old` test targets stop in the same way. The sanitizer and coverage targets do not check the variable.

rows.name: INGEST_PYTHON_VERSION
rows.table: 5.1 `GNUmakefile` and the scripts that it runs

cells.Set by: Nobody by default. Developers may override it.
cells.Values and default: A Python version that `uv` (the Python package tool) accepts for `--python`, for example `3.12.7`. The makefile does not check it. `make INGEST_PYTHON_VERSION=value` also works. Unset: the value of `TOKENIZER_PYTHON_VERSION`, `3.12.7` by default. Empty: the makefile keeps the empty text, and `--python` gets no version.
cells.Effect: Selects the Python version of the two ingest environments, `ingest/export/.venv` and `ingest/runtime/.venv`. The target `ingest-deps` passes it to `uv sync --frozen --python`. When `IN_NIX_SHELL` is set, `ingest-deps` skips `uv` and the value has no effect. `make python-deps`, `make deb` and `make deb-host` also run `ingest-deps`. A comment in `GNUmakefile` says that without `--python`, `uv sync` uses the newest Python of the host.

hints.problem: The rows record pinned versions: Python 3.12.7, uv 0.9.5 and cabal 3.16.0.0. README.dependencies.md already records the same three pins and the steps to change them. .github/AGENTS.md lists README.dependencies.md and README.ci.md as the files to update when a pin changes. After this change a routine pin bump must also edit README.environment.md, and no check reports a miss.
hints.suggested: In the 5 rows replace the version number with a pointer, for example in PYTHON_VERSION: "Python version text with major, minor and patch numbers. [README.dependencies.md](README.dependencies.md) records the pinned value." Keep TRON_HOST_MIN_TRON as it is: its default `2.0.0~1tc6` is recorded nowhere else.

rows.name: NPROC_BUILD
rows.table: 5.1 `GNUmakefile` and the scripts that it runs

cells.Read by: `make`, the Nix build `tron-cmake-test-build`, CI workflows (`GNUmakefile`, `bin/ci/ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh`, `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix` and 2 more files)
cells.Set by: CI workflows, the Nix build and `bin/bsub-build`.
cells.Values and default: Positive integer, a number of parallel jobs. `GNUmakefile` passes the text to `-j` without a check. `bin/ci/ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh` accepts only digits with no leading `0`. `make NPROC_BUILD=4` also works. Unset: `GNUmakefile` uses the smaller of 16 jobs and the `nproc` output. `bin/ci/ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh` stops with the error `NPROC_BUILD is required`.
cells.Effect: `GNUmakefile` adds `-j <value>` to the flags of `make` and to its `cmake --build` commands, except the one that builds IWYU (the include-what-you-use tool). In the Nix build `tron-cmake-test-build`, the job count is the smaller of `NIX_BUILD_CORES` and this value. For a build on an LSF worker (`REMOTE`), the local value does not reach the worker. `bin/bsub-build` sets the variable there to the value of `REMOTE_BUILD_CORES`. Two CI workflows and `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix` set 16 jobs.

rows.name: PRESET_STAMP
rows.table: 5.1 `GNUmakefile` and the scripts that it runs

cells.Values and default: File path. This is an internal make variable. `GNUmakefile` assigns it and ignores an environment value, except when the only goals are `list-tests` or `list-tests-core`. Unset: `gen/.preset_stamp`. When the only goals are `list-tests` or `list-tests-core`, the text is empty.
cells.Effect: An environment value changes no build result. For the goals `list-tests` and `list-tests-core` alone, `make` puts the value into the prerequisite lists of the CMake configure targets. `make` does not build those targets for these goals. The file holds the last CMake preset name, `native` or `darwin`. A changed file makes `make` run CMake configure again. `make PRESET_STAMP=path` on the command line replaces the path for every goal.

rows.name: TOKENIZER_PYTHON_VERSION
rows.table: 5.1 `GNUmakefile` and the scripts that it runs

cells.Set by: CI workflow `publish-deb.yml`, on the `make` command line.
cells.Values and default: A Python version that `uv --python` accepts, for example `3.12.7`. `make` does not check the text. Unset: `3.12.7`. Empty: `make` keeps the empty text. The `uv` commands then get `--python` without a version.
cells.Effect: When `IN_NIX_SHELL` is empty, `make` passes it to `uv` as `--python <value>` in `make tokenize-deps` and in the PyInstaller build of `gen/tokenize_py` (the tokenizer executable that `make deb` packages). That executable embeds this Python interpreter. A changed value makes `make` build `gen/tokenize_py` again. It is also the default of `INGEST_PYTHON_VERSION`. When `IN_NIX_SHELL` is not empty, the recipes do not run `uv`, and `gen/tokenize_py` is a copy of the file that `TRON_TOKENIZE_PY` names. `make TOKENIZER_PYTHON_VERSION=version` also works.

After this change a routine pin bump must also edit README.environment.md, and no check reports a miss.

rows.name: TRON_HOME_ROOT
rows.table: 5.1 `GNUmakefile` and the scripts that it runs

cells.Set by: Nothing in the repository sets it.
cells.Values and default: Path of the directory that holds the home directories. The script compares it as text with the physical path of `HOME` (symbolic links resolved). Unset: `/home`.
cells.Effect: `bin/scratch-dir.sh` creates a build directory below `TRON_SCRATCH_USERS` only when the physical path of `HOME` is below this directory and the checkout is below `HOME`. The part of the `HOME` path after this directory names the user folder below `TRON_SCRATCH_USERS`. A value with a trailing slash never matches. The script does not resolve symbolic links in the value. When the comparison fails, a new build directory is a plain directory in the checkout, not a link. `GNUmakefile` runs the script.

rows.name: TRON_SCRATCH_USERS
rows.table: 5.1 `GNUmakefile` and the scripts that it runs

cells.Set by: Nothing in the repository sets it.
cells.Values and default: Path of the directory under which each user has a folder for build output. Unset: `/scratch/users`.
cells.Effect: For each build directory, `bin/scratch-dir.sh` creates `<value>/<HOME below TRON_HOME_ROOT>/tmp/<checkout path below HOME>/<directory>` and puts a symbolic link to it in the checkout. The build directories are `gen`, `gen-deb`, `gen-deb-host`, `gen-tsan`, `gen-asan` and `gen-coverage`. A new build directory is a plain directory in the checkout in 5 cases: `CI` is not empty, `HOME` is not below `TRON_HOME_ROOT`, the checkout is not below `HOME`, `cmake` is missing or older than version 3.24, or the script cannot create the directory.

cells.Set by: Developers. `bin/bsub-build` sets `0` inside the LSF job.
cells.Values and default: Exactly one of `0`, `1`, `sku0`, `sku1`. Spaces around the value are removed. Any other text stops `make` with an error. `make REMOTE=1` also works. Unset: the value of `TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION` (default `0`) for build goals and test goals, and `0` for other goals. Empty: `make` stops with an error.
cells.Effect: `0` runs everything on the local host. `1`, `sku0` and `sku1` send the goals `all`, `build`, `core`, `build-core`, `build-prod`, `build-test`, `build-ingest`, `build-test-host` and `build-test-fpga` to an LSF worker through `bin/bsub-build`. They also add `--remote` to `bin/slice run` for `test`, `test-core`, `test-host`, `test-fpga` and `test-fast`. `sku0` and `sku1` also add `--remote-sku=<value>` (a server class of the test pool). With `1`, `sku0` or `sku1`, `make` stops with an error for goals that run tests directly, for example `run`, `t_<name>`, `test-proxy` and the coverage goals. Other goals run on the local host.

cells.Values and default: Positive integer, a number of cores. Text with a character other than a digit, or the text `0`, stops the script with exit code 2. Unset: 16 cores.
cells.Effect: Sets the number of cores that the LSF build job reserves. The script exports the same number on the worker as `NPROC_BUILD` and `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS`. It also sets the default of `REMOTE_BUILD_MEM`, 8192 MB for each core. A `-jN` flag of `make` replaces this variable with N. A comment in `GNUmakefile` says that GNU make 4.3 sees `-jN` only when N differs from `NPROC_BUILD`. A value with a leading `0` passes the check, and the memory default reads it in base 8.

cells.Set by: Developers, before a build on an LSF worker.
cells.Values and default: A number of MB (megabytes). The script does not check the text. It passes the text to `bsub` in `rusage[mem=<value>]`. Unset: 8192 MB for each core of `REMOTE_BUILD_CORES`. That is 131072 MB for the default of 16 cores.
cells.Effect: Sets the memory that the LSF build job reserves. The script comment says `8 GB per core` for the default, and the log line adds the suffix `M`. The repository holds no LSF configuration that confirms the unit of `rusage[mem=]`. `make` runs `bin/bsub-build` only when `REMOTE` is `1`, `sku0` or `sku1`.
